title: GeoJSON 3D Terrain Overlay
prompt:
Create procedurally generated noise heightmap terrain using Three.js, and overlay hardcoded GeoJSON polygon regions on it.

[Three.js Import Method (Must Be Followed Strictly)]
Use the following importmap in <head>, and import via ES Modules in <script type="module">:
<script type="importmap">
{ "imports": {
    "three": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js",
    "three/addons/": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/examples/jsm/"
} }
</script>
<script type="module">
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { OrbitControls } from 'three/addons/controls/OrbitControls.js';
</script>

[Terrain]
(1) Procedurally generate a 128×128 heightmap using Perlin/Simplex-like noise, and render the grid as a lit Mesh.
(2) Use an elevation-based material with a low-to-high color gradient.

[GeoJSON]
(3) Hardcode a simple FeatureCollection containing exactly 5 Polygon regions (which may represent simplified national borders/administrative regions), with coordinates mapped to the terrain plane's extent.
(4) Project the polygons onto the terrain surface (along the normals or using sampled heights) as a semi-transparent colored overlay layer.
(5) When a region is clicked, highlight that region and display statistics (approximate area, average elevation, etc.; a DOM panel with id="regionStats" may be used).

[Layer Toggles]
(6) id="terrainToggle": toggle the visibility of the terrain Mesh.
(7) id="regionToggle": toggle the visibility of the region overlay layer.

[State Exposure (Required)]
window.__3D_STATE__ = {
  terrainVertices: number,
  regionCount: number,
  selectedRegion: null | number | string,
  maxElevation: number,
  minElevation: number,
  layerVisibility: { terrain: boolean, regions: boolean }
}

Output a single HTML file that can be opened directly in a browser and run.
physics_constraints: Exactly 5 polygon regions from hardcoded GeoJSON
